media_alt: A generative collection of dragon portrait studies with art nouveau and art deco cues, crisp silhouettes, and ornamental line work.
tiles: Geometric ornament and crisp silhouette control
challenge: Creating a decorative portrait series around non-human subjects requires establishing clear silhouette language and ornamental systems that maintain visual coherence across varied compositions. Dragon portraits drawing on art nouveau and art deco traditions demanded controlled line weight, repeatable motif structures, and highlight discipline to ensure each piece reads cleanly at tile scale while offering detailed ornamentation at larger sizes.
approach: Used a generative pipeline to define silhouette structure and motif rhythm for each dragon portrait, then applied in-painting to refine edge discipline, highlight placement, and line weight consistency. The decorative language draws from art nouveau organic curves and art deco geometric precision, creating portraits that balance ornamental richness with compositional clarity. Each piece maintains crisp silhouette legibility as the anchoring design principle.
result: Produced a cohesive portrait set that reads instantly in grid layouts and carries enough ornamental detail for large-format print. The series demonstrates the ability to direct generative tools toward specific art-historical decorative traditions while maintaining consistent quality and visual identity across a collection. The work is suited for print production, editorial illustration, and digital gallery presentation.
